newsitem.title: USA: Raines - US economy alone won't eliminate deficit.
newsitem.headline: Raines - US economy alone won't eliminate deficit.

text.p: White House Budget Director Franklin Raines said Wednesday the U.S. economy by itself will not wipe out the budget deficit and that the five-year budget agreement reached with Congress needed to be implemented.
"The economy is not going to perform so much better that it's going to balance the budget by itself," Raines told reporters.

Raines said he expected "a good result this year" on the budget deficit, but would not give a specific projection. Wall Street analysts have said the deficit could fall below $50 billion at the end of this fiscal year which ends September 30.
He called "absurd" some notions that letting current fiscal policy continue on "automatic pilot" would be better for wiping out the deficit than implementing the budget agreement.

The economy is performing "very well" but in the next few years was not expected to be as strong as in 1997 or 1996, Raines said. "Our economic assumptions that we've been using show moderate economic growth over the next five years, and that moderate growth would be not as strong as the growth that we've had this year or last year," he said.
President Clinton will not sign a tax bill that would explode the deficit in later years, and there were provisions in both Senate and House bills that would do that, Raines said.
